title: Finite stopped chronological maximum histories
statement: Fix a totally ordered set $V$ with least element $\bot$ and a supplied resolution invariant calculus $\nu$ [def-trf-resolution-invariant-calculus-data] on embedded rational pairs [def-trf-labeled-embedded-resolution]. A maximum segment of length $r$ consists of raw histories $H_i$ of length $i$ for $0\leq i\leq r$, extensions $E_i:H_i\subset H_{i+1}$, admissibility of every $H_i$, nonregularity of every $X_{H_i}$ for $i<r$, and the assertion that each $E_i$ is a maximum step [def-trf-admissible-embedded-history]. There exist $r\geq0$ and such a segment with regular final transform, together with labels $l_i$ in $(V\setminus\{\bot\})^{\mathrm{op}}$ equal to the positive greatest values of $\nu_{H_i}$, strictly increasing in that reverse order. Every center is nonempty, regular and nowhere dense in the current strict transform, with coherent ambient and intrinsic ideals. Each intermediate ambient scheme remains smooth, separated and finite type over $\mathbf Q$, and each intermediate strict transform is reduced. The length is zero for regular or empty inputs [def-weil-regular-scheme]. These data constitute a chronological maximum history. This statement does not assert a realization indexed by lower cuts or independence of the length from the choices.

proof.text: Build the constant length-zero history on the input pair. A maximum extension appends to its finite tuple of prefixes using Fin.snoc. Transport the extension and its maximum-step proof together along the endpoint equalities. The admissibility step rule propagates admissibility and the source remains nonregular.

If no finite segment ended regularly, each segment would end nonregularly. Use maximumExists and choice to choose a next extension for each segment. Natural-number dependent recursion constructs one segment at every length, with the chosen last extension connecting consecutive last histories. These last histories and extensions contradict termination. Thus some finite segment has a regular endpoint.

Choose the greatest positive value from each maximum-step proof. StrictProgress on consecutive steps makes the values decrease, so their reverse-order labels increase; Fin.strictMono_iff_lt_succ gives strict monotonicity. MaximumGeometry gives every center clause. NextGeometry gives the geometry at successor stages, and the initial isomorphisms transport the input geometry. A regular input rules out a first nonregular stage. An empty input is locally Noetherian by the finite-type closed immersion in the rational ambient scheme and is stalkwise regular vacuously, so also has length zero.

theorem maximumHistoryChronology_exists {V : Type w} [LinearOrder V] [OrderBot V]
    (ν : ResolutionInvariantCalculus.{u} V) (A : EmbeddedResolutionPair.{u}) :
    ∃ r, Nonempty (MaximumHistoryChronology ν A r)
